policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the lemma as ‘this thing,’ whose demonstrative and definite force distinguishes the qere הַדָּבָר from ketiv דבר.
ASV’s proper-name form ‘Ephai’ reflects the qere עֵיפַי rather than ketiv עופי.
ASV ‘Thou shalt not do this thing’ does not distinguish qere תַּעֲשֵׂה from ketiv תעש; both candidates remain compatible, so the documented qere base retains the projection.
